incident.what: Twice in one day the agent matched a signal to a remembered failure and acted without checking. (1) After a model switch it assumed its watchers had died — as had happened once before — and remounted them; the old ones were alive, producing duplicates. (2) It saw a scheduled job with a bad exit status and a missing log and declared 'this job never ran', informing the owner; the job's own run log showed 14 successful runs and a designed 12-run limit it had honoured.
incident.signal: Duplicate watcher ticks; the job owner's records contradicting the announcement.

root_cause: Peripheral signals (exit codes, presence of system logs, process lists) were used to close a diagnosis instead of to open one.

law.text: Peripheral signals open an investigation; they never close it. Before declaring a long-running thing dead, never-ran, or in need of restart, read the record it writes for itself, and rule out 'completed on purpose'.
checks: the subject's own log/state file was read before any verdict
the 'finished by design' hypothesis was explicitly excluded
watcher registry was read before mounting a watcher

notes: De-identified from a real operating incident. Names, systems and paths removed; the mechanism is kept.
